title: MIT uses AI to create room-temperature stable mRNA vaccine and cut cold-chain costs
key_facts: MIT researchers used an AI agent running Bayesian optimization to find a solid-state mRNA vaccine formulation.
The formulation kept 100% biological activity after more than two months at 37 degrees Celsius; formulations stable for up to one year were also found.
The AI proposed experiments, humans ran them and fed back results; six rounds gave the best formulation.
Vaccines stored this way produced immune responses comparable to existing formulations in mice and crab-eating macaques.
The team expects storage and transport costs could fall by up to 86%.
Safety and effectiveness in humans still need validation; the results were published on 28 Sep 2026 in Nature Biotechnology.
quote_evidence: The solid-state vaccine formulation identified by AGENT maintained 100% biological activity even after being stored at 37 ℃ for more than two months.
As the work is still at the animal‑testing stage, the safety and immune efficacy in humans will require further validation.
why_it_matters_hint: Vaccines that need no deep freezing could reach places without cold storage, if the animal results hold in people.
event_date: Published 28 Sep 2026 in Nature Biotechnology; Reuters report 7 Oct 2026
